evidence.note: Testing apps are exempt from verification but subject to the 100-user cap.

timeToProduction.text: Sensitive scopes only (gmail.send): usually under a week. Restricted scopes (read or modify): about 4–6 weeks including a CASA security assessment, renewed every year.

evidence.label: Docs
evidence.note: Third-party docs (Nango). Google publishes no fixed SLA.

verdict.summary: Reading or modifying mail uses restricted scopes, which need verification plus a paid annual CASA assessment. If your agent only sends mail, gmail.send is merely sensitive and much faster.

callouts.text: Key tip: gmail.send is only sensitive. It needs verification (scope justification and demo video) but no CASA security assessment.
Internal apps (OAuth consent screen set to 'Internal', with the project owned by your Workspace org) skip verification and the 100-user cap, but only your org's users can sign in.
The 100-user cap counts every user who ever authorized the app and can't be reset. In Testing mode, tokens expire after 7 days.
CASA cost depends on the assessor. Nango lists roughly $540–$720 (TAC Security) up to $3,000+ (others), as of August 2025.

evidence.label: Uncertain
evidence.note: Vendor pricing changes and Google doesn't publish it.

steps.title: Create separate Google Cloud projects for dev and prod
steps.detail: Google says to keep testing apps separate from production and submit only the production project.

steps.title: Enable the Gmail API and configure the OAuth consent screen
steps.detail: Set app name, support email, logo, homepage, privacy policy, and authorized domains. Choose External, or Internal if Workspace-only.

steps.title: Pick the narrowest scopes
steps.detail: Map each agent feature to the lightest scope. Use gmail.send if you only send; gmail.readonly or gmail.modify move you to restricted.

steps.title: Create an OAuth client ID and add test users
steps.detail: Create a Web application client with your redirect URIs. Add up to 100 test users.

steps.title: Implement the OAuth flow and test
steps.detail: Build the consent redirect and token exchange, and request offline access for refresh tokens.

steps.title: Verify your domain and publish privacy policy
steps.detail: Brand verification checks that the homepage, privacy policy, and authorized domains belong to you. Verify domain ownership in Google Search Console.

steps.title: Write scope justifications
steps.detail: Explain why each sensitive or restricted scope is needed and why a narrower one won't do.

steps.title: Record the demo video
steps.detail: Show the end-to-end flow including the full consent screen with exact scopes (in English), and each feature using each scope.

steps.title: Submit for verification and wait
steps.detail: Google's Trust & Safety team reviews the submission and may email follow-up questions.

steps.title: (Restricted scopes) Complete CASA security assessment
steps.detail: Google contacts you when it's time. Hire an empanelled assessor, pass the scan and questionnaire, and get a Letter of Validation. Revalidate every year.

drafts.note: Templates to edit. Replace every [bracketed] part, delete what doesn't apply, and only claim features your app actually has. Nothing here is submitted for you.

scopeJustification.text: [App name] lets users ask an AI assistant to send emails on their behalf, for example [replying to a customer or sending a meeting follow-up]. The assistant drafts the message, shows it to the user for approval, and sends it only after the user clicks Send. We request gmail.send because the feature only needs to send mail; we don't read, modify or delete existing messages, so narrower read scopes aren't needed and broader ones would exceed what the feature uses.

scopeJustification.scope: gmail.readonly (only if you truly need reading)
scopeJustification.text: [App name] summarizes [the user's unread messages from the last 24 hours] so the assistant can [draft replies / build a daily briefing]. We need to read message content because [feature] depends on it; gmail.metadata is not enough because [reason, e.g. summaries need the message body]. We don't store message content beyond [retention period], don't use it to train AI models without explicit consent, and handle it under the Google API Services User Data Policy, including Limited Use.

demoVideoOutline: Open the app's homepage and show the URL bar with your verified domain.
Click 'Connect Gmail' and show the full Google consent screen in English, with the app name and each exact scope visible.
Grant access and show the redirect back to your app.
For each requested scope, show the feature that uses it end to end (e.g. the assistant drafting and sending an email after the user approves).
If you use Gmail data for AI, show where users give explicit consent.
Show how a user disconnects the app or deletes their data.
Upload as unlisted on YouTube and paste the link in the verification form.
checklist: Separate production Google Cloud project (not the one used for testing).
Homepage, privacy policy and authorized domains are on a domain verified in Search Console.
Privacy policy is linked from the homepage and covers how Google user data is used.
Requested scopes are the narrowest that work (gmail.send if you only send).
A justification is written for every sensitive or restricted scope.
The demo video shows the consent screen with exact scopes and each feature using each scope.
Data use is checked against the Google API Services User Data Policy (Limited Use).
If using restricted scopes: budget for a CASA assessment and more than one remediation round.

communityNotes.tip: This developer got restricted Gmail scopes verified in about 3 weeks by having every requested scope working before applying and showing all scopes on the consent screen in the demo video. After passing CASA they emailed Google with their case ID instead of waiting.

communityNotes.tip: Their first review was rejected for not meeting Google's granular scope requirements, and Google asked for test credentials before testing the app. The full restricted-scope process, including the CASA scan and questionnaire, took about four weeks.

communityNotes.tip: Each reply from Google's reviewers took 2–3 weeks, and they asked for the demo video again with the OAuth client ID clearly visible. After about three rounds the sensitive-scope request was denied without a specific reason (this was in 2019).
